description: Welcome to Team Pravartaka! We are a passionate group participating in the Shivamogga local event for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, tackling complex space and Earth science problems through creative tech solutions.
summary:
Project Pravartaka is an interactive, web-based systems engineering simulation that transforms the abstract complexities of space mission design into an accessible educational game. We developed a highly optimized Single-Page Application (SPA) where players act as Mission Architects. They choose science objectives, build spacecraft payloads, balance strict engineering budgets (mass, power, data, and cost), and select launch vehicles.

It directly addresses the "Space Mission Design Game" challenge by dynamically calculating orbital mechanics—using the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation and inverse-square laws for power and data—to determine if a mission will actually survive.

This project is important because it gives students a tangible way to experience the high-stakes trade-offs of real aerospace engineering. To take it a step further, our standout feature is the game's built-in compiler, which exports the player's final spacecraft and orbit parameters directly into a real NASA GMAT script, bridging the gap between a casual game and a true engineering tool.
details:
Launch Window is an interactive web game where players act as aerospace systems engineers. You select a scientific goal, build mission segments (Space, Launch, Ground, User), and balance strict engineering budgets (mass, power, cost) to pass a NASA-style design review.

  • Impact: It gamifies complex orbital mechanics, making aerospace engineering accessible and inspiring for students and space enthusiasts.
  • Tools: Built as a lightweight, single-file web application using HTML5, with all CSS and JavaScript integrated directly into one index.html file. It also exports executable scripts to NASA’s GMAT software.
  • Creativity: The game relies on constraint-based design—your scientific choices actively dictate your real-world engineering limitations, turning dense technical specifications into an engaging puzzle.
